defects.title: pending line read from 'the last record', not the record T comes from
defects.detail: STEP 1 retries the pending line of 'the last record'; RUN RECORD carries it 'from the last record'. If a run dies after writing its Started row (no final update), the next run's last record has no pending line, so M drops off the chain. T still comes from the newest record WITH read to, so M is still re-read through the cursor in practice, but requirement (1) 'never dropped' is broken on paper.
defects.fix: Read and carry the pending line from the same record T comes from (the newest inbox record with 'read to').

defects.title: no reconciliation path for a pending message that can no longer be found
defects.detail: Pending leaves only when 'logged now, or noise'. If M is deleted or the search never returns it, it stays pending forever, read to stays pinned and the window grows with every run. Each run then reads every message since M, with an 'original' call each, so cost grows linearly. Nothing ages it out, caps the window or flags it specifically. The only signal is the pending line plus a Partial/Failed status each run, which the morning check would see.
defects.fix: Add a reconcile rule, e.g. pending older than 24h: say 'pending since <time>' in the report and put one line on Akshay's list or the builder queue. Keep it pending, never drop it.

defects.title: time basis mixed
defects.detail: read to uses 'received time'; the window keeps messages 'dated at or after T'. A message whose Date header lags its delivery by more than 30 minutes can fall before T and never be read.
defects.fix: Use received time for both the filter and read to.

contradictions.pending_retry_vs_window: No conflict. The pending retry is mostly redundant because the cursor never passes M, so M is re-read anyway. It matters only when the search misses M (see D2).
contradictions.step6_72h_catchup: No conflict. Catch-up is driven from Notion pitch Activities, so an unlogged pending M isn't in it. Once M logs within 72h of arrival, STEP 6 handles it in that run's read. If M is pending for more than 72h it never gets a loop-in, consistent with the 72h rule but unreported.
contradictions.unbounded_window: Not capped and not reported as its own item, only indirectly (pending line plus Partial/Failed status). See D2.
